lead.headline: Riyadh's Airport Partly Reopens, but Attacks Go On
lead.deck: Two terminals open again more than two weeks after Houthi strikes.
body: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia, a country on the Arabian Peninsula. On Sunday, its main airport, King Khalid International, opened two terminals again. Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 serve flights inside the country and flights abroad. The airport had been out of service for more than two weeks after strikes by the Houthis, an armed group based in Yemen.

The danger has not gone away. Saudi military spokesman Turki al-Malki said forces stopped a Houthi missile and a drone on Sunday. The Houthis warned airlines and passengers that the airport was unsafe and called it a military target.

So the reopening is only a first step. Flight-tracking data showed that air traffic stayed limited, with fewer planes than usual. The fighting also matters far beyond Riyadh, because it is pushing up the price of oil, as our World story explains.

world.headline: Oil Settles at $116.72, Its Highest Since April
world.deck: A new wave of Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia pushed the price up.
body: Oil is sold by the barrel, and Brent crude is the main world price. On Friday, Brent settled at $116.72 a barrel, the highest settling price since 29 April. Over the week it rose about 6%.

The jump came after the Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Defence Ministry, two airports and an Aramco oil site. Analysts said the price shows fear of lost supply, because no loss of barrels has been confirmed.
